panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial T2-weighted FLAIR MRI of a human patient showing a lobulated pineal-region mass with obstructive hydrocephalus, the classic imaging manifestation of pineal germinoma in an article specifically about metachronous pineal germinoma. B: ADC map of the same patient demonstrating restricted diffusion within the pineal mass, a characteristic MRI feature of pineal germinoma. C: Axial post-contrast T1-weighted MRI of the patient showing the enhancing pineal-region germinoma with mass effect on the tectum/midbrain. D: Sagittal post-contrast T1-weighted MRI of the patient demonstrating the enhancing pineal-region mass with tectal/midbrain compression, supporting the pineal germinoma diagnosis.

panels.figure_caption: Histology and immunohistochemistry of the metachronous pineal germinoma. (A) H&E shows sheets of large round cells with clear cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli admixed with dense lymphocytic inflammation. (B) OCT4 and (C) SALL4 show diffuse strong nuclear staining. (F) Pan‐CK highlights focal trophoblastic cells. (G) β‐hCG highlights focal β‐hCG‐positive syncytiotrophoblastic cells. (H) Ki‐67 immunohistochemistry shows a high proliferative index. Scale bars are indicated in each panel.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: H&E-stained biopsy of the pineal lesion showing the lymphocytic infiltrate surrounding large epithelioid (germ) cells, the two-cell pattern characteristic of germinoma; caption and in-text confirm a pineal germinoma. b: PLAP immunohistochemistry of the pineal biopsy with strong positivity in the neoplastic epithelioid cells, confirming pineal germinoma as stated in the caption.

panels.figure_caption: (a) Rather crushed biopsy of the pineal lesion showing lymphocytes surrounding occasional large epithelioid cells. (b) Placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) immunohistochemical staining of the pineal lesion showing strong positivity within the crushed epithelioid cells in keeping with a germinoma.
in_text_mentions: An MRI scan of the head and spine revealed an intracranial mass measuring 3 cm × 3 cm × 3 cm. This mass compressed the cerebral aqueduct resulting in ventriculomegaly. The lesion was a large pineal germinoma confirmed histopathologically containing a small nonenhancing necrotic area (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). There was no radiological evidence of spinal involvement.

plate_findings.evidence: Fragments of normal brain (upper left) with adjacent highly cellular tumor fragments (lower right) (H&E, 10x)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E section from the stereotactic biopsy of the pineal gland germinoma; shows highly cellular tumor tissue next to normal brain, consistent with the histology of pineal germinoma described in the text. B: High-power H&E of the biopsy showing the classic germinoma two-cell pattern (large tumor cells with round nuclei/prominent nucleoli and interspersed lymphocytes), matching the in-text histopathologic description. C: CD117 immunohistochemistry of the pineal germinoma biopsy showing diffuse positivity, as described in the text; supports germinoma diagnosis. D: PLAP immunohistochemistry of the same pineal germinoma biopsy showing patchy positivity, corroborating the diagnosis as stated in the text.
panels.attribution_text: Wong et al. Depression and Nystagmus as the Rare Masquerading Presentations of Pineal Germinoma.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.42497. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Microscopic images of the pineal tumor. (A) Fragments of normal brain (upper left) with adjacent highly cellular tumor fragments (lower right) (H&E, 10x). (B) The tumor cells exhibit round nuclei and prominent nucleoli with lymphocytes seen in between tumor cells (H&E, 40x). The tumor cells are immunopositive to (C) CD117 (40x) and (D) PLAP (40x). H&E, hematoxylin and eosin stain; PLAP, placental alkaline phosphatase
in_text_mentions: Image-guided stereotactic biopsy revealed a pineal gland germinoma. Histopathologic examination (Figure 3) exhibited (1) mild pleomorphism with moderate to large round hyperchromatic nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and moderate cytoplasm; (2) occasional mitotic figures; (3) mild lymphocytic infiltration in the surrounding parenchyma; (4) neoplastic cells, which stained positive with CD 117 diffusely and placental-like alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) patchily at the membranes and cytoplasm; (5) neoplastic cells unstained with synaptophysin and chromogranin.

findings.label: Convergence-retraction nystagmus
findings.evidence: The convergence-retraction nystagmus was the worst in upgaze attempt than other gazes.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the patient's eyes in attempted upgaze showing bilateral upgaze limitation and convergence-retraction nystagmus, the classic Parinaud (dorsal midbrain) syndrome of a pineal region germinoma; caption and in-text explicitly attribute these findings to the case. B: Clinical photograph in primary gaze showing convergence-retraction nystagmus, a dorsal midbrain sign attributed to the patient's pineal germinoma. C: Clinical photograph in downgaze showing convergence-retraction nystagmus, a dorsal midbrain sign attributed to the patient's pineal germinoma.

There was convergence-retraction nystagmus in upgaze, primary gaze, and downgaze. The convergence-retraction nystagmus was the worst in upgaze attempt than other gazes.
in_text_mentions: On ocular examination, his visual acuity was 6/6 bilaterally. Convergence-retraction nystagmus was noted at upgaze where it was the worst, and also at primary gaze and downgaze (Figure 1). Ocular motility was limited in upgaze for both eyes (Figure 1). No Collier’s sign was noted. Pupil examination showed light-near dissociation without relative afferent pupillary defect. Fundus examination revealed bilateral hyperemic and swollen optic discs, which was compatible with papilledema. findings.label: Obstructive hydrocephalus on imaging
findings.evidence: in-text: 'resulting in dilated lateral ventricles and third ventricles' (visual: enlarged lateral ventricles on coronal FLAIR)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Axial post-contrast T1 MRI of a pineal region mass (arrowed) in a patient with pineal germinoma; article title and caption both attribute the mass to pineal germinoma. B: Axial T2-FLAIR image showing the midline pineal region mass (arrowed) consistent with the reported pineal germinoma. C: Coronal T2-FLAIR image showing the arrowed pineal mass with dilated lateral ventricles (obstructive hydrocephalus) as described in the text of this pineal germinoma case. D: Axial T2 image of the pineal mass with an intratumoral fluid level (arrowed), consistent with the hemorrhagic fluid-fluid levels described in the text of this pineal germinoma case. E: Sagittal T2 image showing the pineal region mass with an intratumoral fluid level (arrowed) in the reported pineal germinoma.

The mass extended superiorly to both thalami, inferiorly to the midbrain involving the left cerebral peduncle, and anteriorly to the cerebral aqueduct, resulting in dilated lateral ventricles and third ventricles.
